summary: Sravana Borkataky-Varma is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD ~2011–2016). She held teaching posts at Rice, UNC Wilmington, Harvard, and the University of Houston.

Sravani Kanamarlapudi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied under Richard Salomon, attended the University of Washington in 2019, and was attested as a PhD student at the University of Texas at Austin in 2026.

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Andhra University, Visva-Bharati University (~1957–1962), and completed his PhD at the University of Marburg (~1963–1966). He later served as professor at Aligarh Muslim University (~1977–1997).

Sri Anirvan (1896–1978) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He pursued his education at Sanskrit College and University (~1914–1918), the University of Calcutta (~1918–1920), and the University of Dhaka.
Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan (1932–2019) was an Indology scholar who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Hamburg (~1961–1967). He served there as Privatdozent für Indologie from 1973 to 1997.

Srisa Chandra Vasu (1861–1918) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Government College University, Lahore (BA ~1877–1881), worked as a Vakil at the Allahabad High Court (~1883), and founded the Panini Office in 1891.

Stacey Van Vleet specializes in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Sinology. She studied at the University of Colorado Boulder and Columbia University (PhD attested 2006) under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, holding a post at Columbia attested in 2013.

Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served as an employee of the East India Company (~1795–1824), founded the Zoological Society of London in 1825, and served as its president in 1826.

Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a Sinologist, Indologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Collège de France under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, whom he succeeded in 1832, holding the chair for Chinese and Manchu language and literature until 1873.

Stanislav Grof studied at Charles University (~1951–1956). His career included positions at Johns Hopkins University (1967–1969), the Maryland Psychiatric Research Center (1969–1973), the Esalen Institute (1973–1987), and the California Institute of Integral Studies (1994–2015).

Stanisław Schayer (1899–1941) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as a professor at the University of Warsaw beginning in 1922 and was a member of the Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences.
Stanley Abe is a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held academic posts at Duke University, attested in 1995 and 2004.

Stanley Insler (1937–2019) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Columbia and under Paul Thieme at Yale (PhD ~1957–1963), where he later served as Salisbury Professor (~1974–2012).

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah (1929–2014) was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Ceylon and Cornell University (PhD ~1951–1954), he held faculty positions at Cambridge (1963–1973), Chicago (1973–1976), and Harvard (1976–2001).

Stanley Lombardo is a scholar of philosophy who studied at Loyola University New Orleans, Tulane University, and the University of Texas at Austin (~1967–1972). He served on the faculty at the University of Kansas from ~1976 to 2014.

Stanley Weinstein (1929–2017) was a Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology scholar. Educated at Komazawa University, the University of Tokyo, and Harvard (PhD under Masatoshi Nagatomi), he taught at SOAS (~1968–1976) and served as professor at Yale.

Stanley Wolpert (1927–2019) was an Indology and history scholar. After studying at the City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania, he had a long career at UCLA starting in 1959, later serving as department chair.
Stefan Anacker (1939–2021) was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from ~1964 to 1970 under the guidance of Alex Wayman.

Stefan Baums is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at the University of Washington (~2002–2009) and held research posts at the University of Munich and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~2012).

Stefan Larsson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Stockholm University in 2009 under Per-Arne Berglie, Erik af Edholm, and David Germano, later holding a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley (attested 2012).
